name: Village of Bronxville
gaps: Bronxville sets bulk rules in the text of each district section (no schedule table); front yard may be reduced to the street average in AA/A, not modeled.
FAR schedule requires interpolation between 1,000 sf rows; bands store the row value at each band's lower bound (slightly generous inside a band).
max_impervious_coverage for AAA/AA/A is 100% minus the code's minimum open-space %, not a stated impervious cap; B/C/D have only per-unit usable open space (null).
No separate corner-lot street-side yard: a front yard is required along every street line.
B/C/D accessory setbacks not set separately (null); AAA-A accessory rules come from § 310-8A(4).
No local wetlands, steep-slope or private-tree law found in the Village Code (Ch. 282 covers public trees only).

wetlands.summary: No Village wetlands chapter; filling or diverting a watercourse, floodplain or wetland needs Planning Board site plan approval (§ 310-26A). NYS DEC 100 ft adjacent area applies to state wetlands.

steep_slopes.summary: No steep-slope law; garages may get a special permit closer to the street where slope within 25 ft of the street line is 12-20% (10 ft) or over 20% (5 ft).

trees.summary: Ch. 282 regulates trees on public streets and places only (permit from Superintendent of Public Works); no private tree-removal permit found.

stormwater.summary: Ch. 257: SWPPP required for land development activity disturbing 1 acre or more (or part of a larger plan).

adu.summary: No accessory-apartment provision in Ch. 310; one-family districts allow one dwelling per lot.

general.accessory_structures: In AAA/AA/A: detached garages 10 ft from property lines (10 ft flat / 15 ft pitched, 1 1/2 stories), sheds 5 ft, recreational structures 10 ft; none in front yards or closer to the street than the house; screening required (§ 310-8A(4)).
general.pools: At least 20 ft from any property line and no closer to the street than the house's rear wall (corner lots: may extend to the required front yard on one street); 6 1/2 ft opaque screening (§ 310-8A(4)(b)).
general.notes: New one-family houses and 'material alterations' (FAR +30%, >50% of walls, >7,500 sf, etc.) need Planning Board site plan approval (§ 310-26D). Parking not allowed in front yards beyond a 12 ft driveway; driveways 3 ft from side lines (§ 310-22D).

Residence AAA.name: One-Family Residence AAA District

max_building_coverage.note: All principal and accessory buildings and structures (definition since 2021 includes decks, patios, pools, sheds)

max_impervious_coverage.note: Derived from § 310-8H minimum open space 60%: open space excludes buildings, pools, courts, decks, patios, walks, driveways and parking

max_floor_area.note: § 310-22E Residential FAR Schedule (one- and two-family lots). FAR must be interpolated between rows (e.g. 12,500 sf -> 0.345); bands give the row value at each band's lower bound. Counts all floors of principal and accessory buildings; excludes cellars/basements not a story, up to 400 sf of garage, attics with dormers <= 30% of roof width; spaces over 14 ft high count twice. Houses over 7,500 sf need Planning Board site plan review.

accessory.notes: Detached garages: 10 ft from any property line if max 10 ft (flat roof) / 15 ft (pitched) and 1 1/2 stories; sheds, garden and tool houses 5 ft; recreational structures 10 ft; none in a front yard or nearer the street than the house; all screened by 6 1/2 ft fence/hedge (§ 310-8A(4)(b)-(c), D(5))

Residence AAA.notes: Height for one-family dwellings measured from average finished grade along the street-facing wall to a flat roof or the midpoint between eaves and ridge of a pitched roof (§ 310-3). Front yard along each street line (corner lots have two); may project to 20 ft where walls meet the street at 25 deg+. One side yard 30 ft if no garage; corner lot side yard opposite principal front 30 ft. Pools 20 ft from property lines and behind the house's rear wall.

Residence B.name: Two-Story Multiple Residence B District

max_building_coverage.note: All principal and accessory buildings; Planning Board may allow +10% for garages; roof-deck garages exempt

max_floor_area.note: § 310-22E Residential FAR Schedule (one- and two-family lots). FAR must be interpolated between rows (e.g. 12,500 sf -> 0.345); bands give the row value at each band's lower bound. Residence B.notes: One-family houses permitted (any A-district use). 2,750 sf of lot per dwelling unit; average depth 100 ft. Front may project to 15 ft and a one-family side wall to 10 ft where walls are angled 25 deg+. 400 sf usable open space per unit; buildings max 160 ft long.

max_building_coverage.note: All principal and accessory buildings; Planning Board may allow +10% for garages; roof-deck garages exempt

max_floor_area.note: § 310-22E Residential FAR Schedule (one- and two-family lots). Residence C.notes: Side yard = 1/2 the height of the facing wall, min 12 ft (one-family side wall may project to 10 ft where angled 25 deg+). 1,750 sf of lot per dwelling unit. FAR schedule applies by § 310-22E to any lot whose principal use is a one- or two-family dwelling.

Residence D.notes: Side yard = 1/2 the facing wall height, min 12 ft, for buildings up to 36 ft; taller buildings 25 ft + 1/6 of wall height. 1,500 sf of lot per dwelling unit (age-restricted facilities: 60,000 sf lot, 750 sf/unit, own yards). Buildings max 180 ft long.
